chunks: The Day the hypocrites, men and women, will say to the believers, 'Wait for us that we may borrow a little light from your light,' they will be told, 'Go back, and look for your light.' A wall shall be raised between them in which there will be a door. Within it will be benevolence and retribution without.

key_terms.النُّور: Light, symbolizing spiritual illumination and faith
key_terms.الْمُنَافِقُونَ: The hypocrites, those who outwardly profess faith but inwardly conceal disbelief

ai.seo_question: What happens to the hypocrites on the Day of Judgment regarding their light and separation from believers?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'light' (nur) borrowed by the hypocrites is often interpreted as the spiritual radiance of the Ahl al-Bayt and the faithful, highlighting the necessity of true internal conviction over superficial association. The wall (sur) with its inner mercy and outer punishment symbolizes the definitive separation between the elect and the hypocrites, a concept reinforced by the Imam Ali's narration that the hypocrites will seek refuge in the light of the Prophet but will be cast back due to their lack of genuine faith. This scene underscores the eschatological reality that spiritual status is determined by the depth of one's connection to divine truth, not merely by outward appearance.
